approach.method_basis: The Parent breeds fresh molecular graphs from a bounded population of high-scoring accepted molecules. Score-quantile parent draws feed connected-fragment crossover, optional finishing mutation and ordinary graph-mutation walks. Direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange is disabled; stable canonical identities, duplicate rejection and a sulfur gate relative to the original scored generating parents control admission. Every fresh pool contains a surplus of offspring. A count-Tanimoto Gaussian process refits all current accepted observations and supplies correlated residual draws. A frozen synthetic-pretrained TabPFN regressor, conditioned on the same standardized observations through a fixed Gaussian count projection, supplies the active score location. Sequential masked maxima select the batch, and real feedback updates the archive and greedy survivor population.
approach.novelty: Remove the active pretrained predictive location while retaining its full model computations and existing environment. The same original correlated residuals will instead be added to the original count-GP means; external means remain passive comparisons. This creates a control for the completed pretrained-location recipe within its own environment. The frozen brief has no same-Parent siblings. Earlier composite-selector and locally fitted tree controls tested different modules and cannot supply this location-specific answer. The control predicts that the GP ordering advantage observed on the Parent’s accepted molecules can translate into stronger accepted search, while the complete matched panel decides the total contribution.

observed_bottleneck: The limiting behavior is a genuinely exposed pretrained score location that orders its actually selected molecules worse than the concurrently computed original count-GP location. On code Parent n-3062f0c87203, all fifteen task sessions and all three summary.json/run.log pairs completed successfully: seed macro scores are 0.561744573032384, 0.52243671838943 and 0.550141130320776; mean 0.5447741405808634 and population SD 0.016490002896889726. The archived analysis and frozen catalog report 435 full 160-member pools, 435 external fits and 2994 strict same-actual-mask choice flips among 4350 selections. On the same actual accepted identities, external versus original GP MSE is 0.007415991013485042 versus 0.006551303170446416, pair-order accuracy 0.6349149415863906 versus 0.6893830703012912, and batch Spearman 0.35278052022601825 versus 0.48433302836152137; fourteen of fifteen sessions lose both ordering measures. More relative parent wins and incumbent advances coexist with weaker absolute offspring quality, so those counts do not repair the ranking prediction. The raw endpoint difference of -0.05167897370782667 against n-1744a1494180 is separately descriptive: the frozen catalog has paired_complete=false, matched_seeds=[] and paired_mean_delta=null because the environment locks differ. The locally fitted CART replacement n-7922cfd1903a changed both learner and function law and is a distinct counterexample, not evidence that this exact retained-residual control has already been tested. A same-environment removal is needed to answer the active-location contribution gap.

literature_review.conclusion: Reuse the recorded n-3062f0c87203 literature/model-provenance review because this ticket retains exactly its original checkpoint, package, projection, full accepted contexts, preprocessing and residual consumer; only the active location is removed. I read the archived external implementation, asset/provenance records and complete Parent summaries/run logs, and directly reopened the primary Nature article, frozen official model card, official 2.1.3 release and Gaussian projection documentation. Nature returned the article despite a cookie-error URL. This PLAN ran no new search queries; queries=[] is intentional and the source node retains its historical searches, newer-model discussion and deferred alternatives. Do not upgrade or search a new model recipe to repair a fixed-location contribution control. The inspected code supplies the existing GP mean and exact common residuals before external allocation, making this a concrete removal boundary; same-label ranking failure supplies a reason to expect benefit, while only a complete exact-environment matched panel can answer total contribution. General literature gains, model execution and the historical cross-lock endpoint difference do not answer that question.

finding_summary.headline: Pretrained active location has negative matched contribution; GP ordering improves despite calibration limits
finding_summary.insights:
This complete comparison closes the active-location contribution gap for the frozen pretrained recipe inside the retained count-GP residual selector: its active location harms this matched panel at the registered 0.002 descriptive scale. Full model work remains in the control, so the gain cannot be assigned to skipping neural computation or changing the environment. Ordering, calibration and search progress are distinct: improved same-label ordering accompanies stronger absolute accepted progress even though squared error is slightly worse and one session loses both ordering measures. Actual changed identities enter later fits and breeding, but those joins do not identify mediation, and unused passive alternatives have no labels or continued histories. The projection, weights, preprocessing and raw conversion still constitute one recipe; their individual effects and transfer remain open.

All current trajectories reproduce earlier original-GP trajectories exactly, so they add a compatible treatment-versus-control answer rather than independent replication. The earlier cross-lock endpoint comparison remains unpaired, and its original Anchor performance target is not achieved or retroactively repaired. The molecular assessment associates higher labels with useful compact aromatic/carbonyl and cyclic-amine contexts in several series, while reactive local bonds, strained ring arrangements and unspecified stereochemistry persist. Better scalar search scores therefore leave chemical plausibility and broader generator capability unresolved. This bounded control supplies its component answer without settling those wider gaps.
finding_summary.results:
The control completed all 15 task/seed sessions. Mean final Top-1 rose from 0.544774 to 0.596453, a paired gain of 0.051679: all three seed means improved, 14 of 15 endpoints rose, and median_2 seed 1 fell by 0.014163. Seed dispersion increased from 0.016490 to 0.033970. The location change reached real feedback: all 435 fresh-pool sets changed, with 2777 strict same-mask winner disagreements and 2457 accepted identities absent from the passive external batch. Both predictors still refitted 435 times on complete accepted contexts; 14 external preprocessing overflow warnings remained visible, with finite outputs and no numerical fallbacks.

On the control's same 4350 accepted labels, GP pair-order accuracy was 0.709552 versus 0.663999 for the passive external mean, and mean batch Spearman was 0.525513 versus 0.422185. Both ordering measures improved in 14 sessions; zaleplon_mpo seed 2 was a counterexample. GP MSE was slightly worse, 0.011213 versus 0.011061, contradicting the lower-error prediction in 11 sessions. Accepted offspring scores increased from 0.298274 to 0.372050 and cumulative incumbent gain from 5.044230 to 5.819415, while local parent wins fell from 703 to 648 and sequential incumbent advances from 268 to 255. Stronger absolute progress therefore did not require more relative wins or uniformly better squared error.

molecular.headline: Compact aromatic carbonyl frameworks and cyclic amines coexist with reactive attachments, strained closures and unspecified stereochemistry
molecular.overall_character: Node n-fe734eb5c1df produces ring-rich aromatic amides/ketones, nitrogen-rich oxo/thioxo heterocycles, halogenated aryl/cyclic amines, azaarene-linked cyclic diones, and fluorinated carbonyl/imino systems. Typical leading molecules are of medicinal-molecule size, although much larger concatenations and tiny fragments also occur. Different seeds reach recognizably different families, supporting moderate overall structural diversity; high-label series within a seed often remain close relatives. The digest's ring-closure incidence spans 0.9598 to 0.9897 and aromatic-token incidence spans 0.9517 to 0.9782. These are molecule-level SMILES-text incidences, not perceived ring counts or aromatic-atom fractions. All five optimizer sets have charge-marker and stereocentre-marker incidence 0.0. Neutral notation nevertheless includes clearly protonatable aliphatic amines; amine chemistry is not absent. Potentially stereogenic saturated, fluorinated and bridged arrangements remain unspecified. Conventional carbonyls, aryl halogens and saturated cyclic amines coexist with direct N/O/S-halogen connections, nitroso and peroxide attachments, compressed unsaturated rings and difficult bridges. Synthetic plausibility is therefore questionable and ordinary drug-likeness weak overall, with substantial variation among individual molecules. In particular, the leading saturated cyclic-diamine/thioether example is more conventional than several other leaders. All 15 Child and 15 assigned published n-3062f0c87203 Parent trajectories were present and read. Each node provides 900 records per objective, including 870 optimizer records across Search seeds 0, 1 and 2; no task or trajectory path is missing. The streams contain accepted evaluated structures, and do not show every unselected pool member or rejected proposal. The request reports child_complete=true and paired_complete=true, matched_seeds=[0,1,2], with no profile-mismatched seeds for this code-Parent comparison. This current pairing does not repair the historical cross-lock n-3062f0c87203 versus n-1744a1494180 comparison, which remains unpaired under the bound conditions. Published Parent structures below are the assigned baseline; the compact Parent assessment in the brief was expanded through its public evidence_index node path. Original qualitative gaps were recorded in Development n-c55c3d520a2c, carried through profile-1 n-62daf219c70a and n-1744a1494180, and re-observed in n-3062f0c87203 under its changed Candidate environment. Their historical conditions and effects are not pooled into the present molecular reading. All complete SMILES in cited_smiles are Child molecules in the digest or the request's trusted citation_trajectory_paths; Parent-only molecules are described from the assigned published paths. Read-only structural aids and all trajectory hashes are retained in .slots/L01-resume-20261003/r31-slot2-molecular/trajectory_review.json. Scores below are existing labels, rounded for readability. Scalar labels provide no decomposition identifying a missing exact reference substructure and do not measure synthesis, stability, binding or stereochemical penalties. These are output associations, not activation decisions or attribution to a search component.

per_task.generated_character: Mostly compact fused indole/azaindole-like aromatic frameworks joined through carboxamide, N-hydroxycarboxamide, ketone or adjacent oxo/thioxo groups to phenyl or pyridyl rings. Alkyl, vinyl, methoxy and halogen decorations are common. Seed 0 emphasizes an azaindole N-hydroxycarboxamide series, seed 1 a substituted ring-N-halogen carboxamide series, and seed 2 indole-linked oxo/thioxo compounds and cross-linked relatives. Digest ring-closure/aromatic-token incidences are 0.9736/0.969 and mean SMILES length is 41.9. Several carbonyl-linked frameworks look synthetically conceivable, but ring N-F/N-Cl, N-S and haloalkyl-ether substitutions make many emitted relatives questionable. The Parent also retains compact aromatic carbonyl families: its seed 0 leader is a fused azaaryl ketone, seed 1 an N-fluorinated azaaryl amide, and seed 2 an N-amino ketone with a chloromethyl ether.
liabilities: Direct ring N-F/N-Cl and N-S bonds, halomethyl ethers and benzylic halogens require environment-specific stability and synthesis scrutiny; ordinary aryl halogens also occur and are distinct.
N-hydroxycarboxamides are recognizable chemistry, but their appearance at high labels does not validate the neighboring ring-halogen or cross-linked topology.
Some cross-linked late relatives contain potentially stereogenic arrangements without specified stereochemistry; simple aromatic leaders need not have such centres.
missing_features: Low-label fragments and enlarged concatenations fail to preserve the compact conjunction of fused aromatic and carbonyl-linked aryl regions seen in the high-label series.

Leading excerpts do not demonstrate a broad supply of conventional alternative azaaryl/carbonyl arrangements free of reactive attachments; the scalar labels do not specify a particular absent reference scaffold.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The shared initial methoxyindole aryl amide has label 0.305105. Child seed maxima are 0.459357, 0.474117 and 0.436954, versus published Parent maxima 0.433013, 0.448130 and 0.427621 in seed order. The high-label Child structures retain an aromatic fused region and a carbonyl-linked second aromatic region; ClCl has label 0.0. Ring richness alone is insufficient: the larger concatenated indole/carboxamide molecule at seed 0 evaluation 42 has label 3.861219282660785e-08. Several seed 1 methoxy/halomethyl and ring-halogen rearrangements share label 0.447848, so peripheral string novelty does not necessarily change reward. The observations support compact, coordinated aromatic/carbonyl context over fragmentation or indiscriminate concatenation, without identifying an exact missing target motif or isolating the benefit of N-hydroxylation.

per_task.generated_character: The seeds occupy different nitrogen- and oxygen-rich ring families. Seed 0 reaches a comparatively compact fused oxo/thioxo nitrogen heterocycle joined to an azaarene, bearing an O-F substituent and fluorinated N-sidechains. Seed 1 keeps a larger ether-linked azaaromatic/cyano series with cyanate, bromoalkyl and S-Br attachments. Seed 2 contains carbonyl-bearing aromatic/imine frameworks joined through a nitroso-substituted amine region, with compressed unsaturated small-ring closures. Digest ring-closure/aromatic-token incidences are both 0.9713; mean SMILES length is 58.5 and the maximum is 191. The published Parent leaders are substantially more elaborated linked heterocyclic diones with polyene, ene-yne, ether or carbonyl appendages. Ring abundance is clear in both nodes, but many particular connectivities and local attachments are chemically questionable.
liabilities: The leading seed 0 O-F bond is a heteroatom-halogen attachment, distinct from ordinary aryl fluorination, and its high label does not establish chemical stability.
Seed 1 includes S-Br, cyanate and bromoalkyl environments; seed 2 includes nitroso groups and crowded unsaturated small-ring closures.
Large linked frameworks can carry redundant rings and appendages; compactness improves in the leading seed 0 family without resolving all feasibility questions.
missing_features: Floor-scoring fragments lack the connected heteroaromatic and carbonyl-bearing regions found in higher-label structures; additional arbitrary aromatic concatenation does not reliably recreate that arrangement.
The leading series do not consistently supply chemically conventional alternative decoration-bearing ring frameworks with the same useful heteroatom/carbonyl context.
Explicit stereochemical identity is absent where saturated bridge or fluorinated-sidechain environments could require it; no score penalty for that omission is demonstrated.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The shared initial aromatic dione has label 0.548381. Child maxima are 0.856148, 0.620438 and 0.644234, versus Parent 0.620604, 0.609789 and 0.606978. Tiny C=C has label 0.5, while the long Child concatenation at seed 0 evaluation 53 has label 0.562821. The much higher seed 0 labels associate with an organized nitrogen-rich fused oxo/thioxo/azaarene arrangement rather than maximal graph growth. Several distinct fluorinated sidechain variants share exactly 0.8561477222467935, showing a local plateau. This does not establish that O-F or thiocarbonyl groups cause the higher label: different seed families have different contexts and no score-component breakdown is supplied.

per_task.generated_character: Leading structures combine halogenated aryl regions with aliphatic nitrogen centres. Seed 1 has a medium saturated cyclic diamine, an aryl substituent at its saturated carbon, a phenethyl-linked second aryl ring, and methylthio decoration: a comparatively conventional medicinal-chemistry framework. Seed 0 has a bridged tertiary amine with phenolic/fluorinated aryl groups and tight ring closures. Seed 2 retains a chroman-like aryl region and aminomethyl-substituted amine linkage to an unsaturated small nitrogen ring. Digest ring-closure/aromatic-token incidences are 0.9782/0.9724; halogen incidence is 0.9828 and mean SMILES length is 53.2. The Parent also reaches aryl/cyclic-amine chemistry, including azetidine-containing and larger annulated structures. Basic cyclic nitrogen is already prominent in both nodes; no absence of amines can be inferred from zero charge markers.
liabilities: The seed 1 S-F analogue and seed 2 haloalkyl attachments add local reactivity concerns to otherwise recognizable aryl/amine chemistry.
Seed 0 tight bridged closures and seed 2 unsaturated small nitrogen rings need geometric feasibility assessment; sanitizable connectivity alone does not supply it.
Highly halogenated, crowded and multiply basic examples can be difficult medicinal chemistry; no physicochemical or synthesis validation accompanies their high labels.
missing_features: Low-label N-sulfonyl/N-acyl examples do not present the same accessible aliphatic-amine and connected aryl arrangement as the high-label families.
Potentially stereogenic diamine carbons and bridged aryl/amine centres lack explicit stereochemical identity.

Useful cyclic amines are available, but plausible alternative topologies preserving their aryl/nitrogen relationship are inconsistent across seeds; more rings or more halogens alone is not the missing capability.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Child maxima are 0.991254, 0.9999994532254913 and 0.981798, versus Parent 0.940596, 0.912544 and 0.961792. The cited low-label N-chloroamide/N-sulfonyl cyclic nitrogen structure has label 0.000167. In contrast, the leading series present accessible aliphatic nitrogen alongside connected hydrophobic aryl regions; halogens alone do not explain the gradient because both extremes contain them. A saturated diamine example already has label 0.962711 at seed 1 evaluation 100. The later methylthio diamine has 0.9999994532254913, while its S-F relative has 0.9999970978615854: a high label does not require the S-F attachment. Other high-label seed families have difficult topology, so there is no single obligatory ring system. The labels are supplied objective values, not independently demonstrated docking poses or binding measurements.

per_task.generated_character: Larger aromatic azaarene/cyclic-dione combinations dominate the higher-label molecules. Seed 2 keeps a quinoline-like aromatic region linked to fused lactam/dione and aliphatic-amine rings, varying alkyl length and ring spacing. Seed 1 has an ethoxy azaarene connected to an O/N ring and a dione nitrogen ring. Seed 0 produces more crowded fused aromatic N-N and cyclic-dione frameworks. Digest ring-closure/aromatic-token incidences are 0.9897/0.9782, mean SMILES length 54.0 and halogen incidence only 0.1552. The chemistry is therefore strongly cyclic/aromatic without being uniformly halogenated. The Parent similarly reaches aryl-linked cyclic diones, with lactone, ether, amine or larger nitrogen-ring arrangements. Carbonyl and cyclic nitrogen chemistry is recognizable, but more elaborate closures and N-N variants weaken confidence in synthesis and geometry.
liabilities: Dense fused or medium-ring nitrogen closures may be demanding to synthesize and can constrain geometry; familiar carbonyl fragments alone do not certify the whole graph.
N-N/N-S and N-hydroxy relatives occur among late variants and add environment-dependent chemical concerns.
Large concatenations and close peripheral variants can add complexity without recovering the strongest observed functional arrangement.
missing_features: The low-label simple aryl ether and tiny fragments lack the conjunction of azaaromatic and carbonyl-bearing nitrogen-ring regions present in high-label molecules.

Chemically independent conventional connectivities preserving that conjunction remain limited among the leading excerpts; the many close alkyl and ring-spacing variants do not demonstrate broad useful alternatives.
Some seed 0 and seed 1 saturated junctions lack explicit stereochemical identity; the leading seed 2 planar/unsaturated arrangement need not have a tetrahedral stereocentre.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The shared initial aromatic dione has label 0.167839. Child maxima are 0.214451, 0.221410 and 0.232334, versus Parent 0.208271, 0.235573 and 0.212956: the seed 1 Child maximum is below its Parent, so this chemistry comparison is not uniformly favorable. Ethoxybenzene has label 0.100012 and NO has 0.0; the high-label conjunction includes a larger coordinated azaarene, cyclic dione and nitrogen arrangement. Local spacing matters modestly: the seed 2 ring-expanded dione/amine relative has 0.232334 versus 0.230925 for the shorter ring, while either an extra sidechain carbon or a methylene spacer has 0.225706. This is incremental refinement of a repeated family, not evidence that arbitrary molecular enlargement is useful or that the exact missing similarity motif can be inferred.

per_task.generated_character: Leading molecules are compact nitrogen-rich carbonyl/imino or dicarbonyl frameworks with fluoroalkyl groups and aryl or unsaturated carbocyclic attachments. Seed 0 progresses from fused azaheterocycles to an aromatic-labelled enlarged nitrogen ring connected to a methoxy/fluorinated carbocycle and an unsaturated small nitrogen ring. Seed 1 retains a phenolic aryl-linked dione with N-F, N-O and fluoroalkyl attachments. Seed 2 has a carbonyl/imino fused nitrogen system with a compressed small-ring closure and a fluorinated hydroxy carbocycle. Digest ring-closure/aromatic-token incidences are 0.9598/0.9517, halogen incidence 0.8839 and mean SMILES length 47.1. The Parent includes an enlarged aromatic-labelled N-fluorinated dione ring, a nonaromatic bridged dione family, and a fused nitrogen/dione family. Distinct connectivities exist, but credible ring geometry and conventional nitrogen substitution remain inconsistent.
liabilities: Direct N-F and N-O connections, and the low-label N-N-F replacement, differ chemically from ordinary carbon-bound fluorine and cannot be treated as interchangeable decoration.
Aromatic-labelled enlarged nitrogen rings, unsaturated small nitrogen rings and compressed fused closures need structural feasibility assessment.
Peroxide-linked elaborated relatives and haloalkyl substitution add local reactivity and synthesis concerns that are not tested by these scalar labels.
missing_features: Low-label fragments and concatenations fail to reproduce a compact arrangement of fluorinated substituents with nitrogen/carbonyl or imino regions.
Leading structures do not consistently provide conventional, geometrically credible alternative ring frameworks while preserving the useful local atom environments.

Fluorinated saturated carbons and ring junctions remain stereochemically unspecified; labels alone do not establish whether stereochemical resolution or a particular absent reference motif would improve the objective.

Isolated F has 1.1043196211273875e-26; the extended peroxide-linked heterocycle at seed 0 evaluation 80 has 3.862281475007376e-18. transferable_gaps.gap: The generator inconsistently preserves conventional local bond environments while retaining useful aromatic, carbonyl and amine frameworks.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Offer bond-environment-aware alternatives that preserve useful relationships learned from current accepted feedback. Distinguish carbon-bound halogens and conventional amine/carbonyl/sulfur environments from reactive heteroatom connections, rather than banning an entire element or functional-group class. Evaluate the alternatives with legal current-session feedback; neither synthesis nor a universal score benefit follows from this association.

Aromatic labels and graph sanitization do not supply conformational evidence. Preserve ordinary small, fused and medium rings where appropriate; a blanket ring ban and a guaranteed endpoint benefit are unsupported.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
